passages.provision_quote: (2) procedure for each school to allow a: (A) parent or guardian of a student enrolled in the school; or (B) community member: (i) within the school district; or (ii) within the school district in which the charter school is located; to submit a request to remove material from the school library that is obscene (as described in IC 35-49-2-1) or harmful to minors (as described in IC 35-49-2-2); and
passages.note: HB 1447 also amends Muncie schools flexibility, vendor-survey privacy, political neutrality, and obscenity-dissemination law in the same act; no Donato statement ties her vote or sponsorship to the library provision specifically.
Final-passage conference committee vote on a multi-subject education bill; does not isolate the library-book provision, and it is not near-unanimous (39-10).
Bill-tracking page names Donato as a Senate sponsor of HB 1447; its own digest excerpt describes the third-party-vendor-survey provision, not the library-book provision.
passages.actor_quote: Sponsored by: Sen. Stacey Donato, Sen. Jeff Raatz.

rows.reasoning: Donato sponsored and voted Yea on HB 1447 (2023), which added a chapter letting a parent or community member request removal of school library material that is obscene or harmful to minors, reviewed by the governing body at its next public meeting; but the same act also enacted several unrelated education provisions, so the vote and sponsorship are multi-subject and, without any Donato statement tying her support to the library provision, cannot establish whether she holds 'remove a challenged book only if a review committee of educators and parents finds it unsuitable', 'pull any book a parent challenges until it has been reviewed', or 'remove any book a parent or community member reports as inappropriate, for all students'.
needs_source: Donato floor statement, press release, or testimony specifically addressing HB 1447's school library provision or the library-book-challenge policy question
